title: Estate Planning Starter Checklist
description: A systematic framework for young adults to assess their current estate planning needs, identify priority documents, and create an actionable plan for protecting themselves and their families through wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and healthcare directives
learning_objectives: Assess which estate planning documents are essential for your current life stage
Document current status of wills, trusts, beneficiaries, and incapacity protection
Prioritize estate planning actions based on personal situation and risk
Create a timeline and budget for obtaining necessary documents
Identify appropriate agents, guardians, and beneficiaries for your situation

inputs.label: Current Life Stage
inputs.help_text: Select the option that best describes your current family situation

inputs.label: Estimated Total Assets
inputs.help_text: Combined value of retirement accounts, savings, property, vehicles, life insurance

inputs.label: Do you have a current will?
inputs.help_text: A will that reflects your current wishes and situation

inputs.label: When was your will last updated?
inputs.help_text: Month and year of last update (if applicable)

inputs.label: Do you have a healthcare directive/living will?
inputs.help_text: Document specifying medical treatment preferences and naming healthcare proxy

inputs.label: Healthcare Proxy/Agent Name
inputs.help_text: Person authorized to make medical decisions if you're incapacitated

inputs.label: Do you have a financial power of attorney?
inputs.help_text: Document authorizing someone to handle finances if you're incapacitated

inputs.label: Financial POA Agent Name
inputs.help_text: Person authorized to manage your finances if you're incapacitated

inputs.label: Number of Minor Children
inputs.help_text: Children under 18 for whom you have parental responsibility

inputs.label: Have you formally designated guardians in a will?
inputs.help_text: Legal guardians who would raise your children if you die or become incapacitated

inputs.label: Do you have retirement accounts (401k, IRA, etc.)?
inputs.help_text: Any employer or individual retirement accounts

inputs.label: When did you last review ALL beneficiary designations?
inputs.help_text: Retirement accounts, life insurance, POD/TOD accounts

inputs.label: Total Life Insurance Coverage
inputs.help_text: Combined death benefit of all life insurance policies

inputs.label: Do you have a trust?
inputs.help_text: Revocable living trust, testamentary trust, or other trust structure

inputs.label: Trust Type
inputs.help_text: Type of trust if you have one

inputs.label: Who knows where your documents are located?
inputs.help_text: List people who know document locations and have access if needed

calculations.label: Estate Planning Priority Score
calculations.formula: Calculate based on life_stage, age, assets_total, num_children, has_will, has_healthcare_directive, has_financial_poa
calculations.help_text: Higher score = higher urgency for estate planning

calculations.label: Estimated Probate Cost (if no planning)
calculations.help_text: Typical probate costs 3-7% of estate; using 5% midpoint

calculations.label: Estimated Planning Cost
calculations.formula: Calculate based on life_stage and has_trust
calculations.help_text: Cost to obtain necessary documents for your situation

calculations.label: Net Benefit of Planning
calculations.help_text: Financial benefit of estate planning (not counting family peace of mind)

outputs.label: 30-Day Action Plan
outputs.description: Specific steps to take this month

outputs.label: Agent Selection Guidance
outputs.description: Who to consider for healthcare proxy, financial POA, guardians

outputs.label: Cost Comparison
outputs.description: Planning cost vs. potential probate cost

level_2_important: Basic will (if assets > $25,000 or in serious relationship)
level_3_beneficial: Trust consideration (if minor children + life insurance OR assets > $500,000)
Beneficiary review (if any retirement accounts or life insurance)
level_4_advanced: Irrevocable trust (if estate tax concern or asset protection needed)

scenarios.name: Recent Graduate (Age 23)
scenarios.description: Single, no dependents, modest assets, starting career

scenarios.name: Young Parents (Ages 30/32)
scenarios.description: Married with two young children, growing assets

scenarios.name: Divorced Parent (Age 38)
scenarios.description: Single parent, one child, need to update documents

scenarios.name: Engaged Couple (Ages 27/28)
scenarios.description: Planning marriage, want to start estate planning

validation_rules.warning_message: CRITICAL: You have minor children but no designated guardians. This should be your top priority.
IMPORTANT: At 18+, your parents have no automatic authority to make medical decisions. You need a healthcare directive.

validation_rules.condition: If life_insurance_amount > 0 and beneficiaries_reviewed != 'Within past year'
validation_rules.warning_message: REVIEW NEEDED: Life insurance beneficiaries should be reviewed annually and after all major life events.

validation_rules.condition: If has_will and will_updated_date contains years ago > 3
validation_rules.warning_message: UPDATE NEEDED: Wills should be reviewed every 3-5 years and after major life changes.

validation_rules.condition: If life_stage includes 'relationship' or 'married' and not has_will
validation_rules.warning_message: IMPORTANT: Serious relationships require estate planning. Unmarried partners have no automatic inheritance rights.

feedback_messages.well_planned: Your estate planning is in good shape! Remember to review annually and update after major life events.
feedback_messages.basic_complete: You have basic protections in place. Consider adding {recommended_documents} to strengthen your plan.
feedback_messages.critical_gaps: You have critical estate planning gaps. Priority actions: {critical_actions}
feedback_messages.no_planning: You currently have no estate planning documents. Start with healthcare directive and financial POA this month.
feedback_messages.parents_urgent: As a parent, guardian designation is URGENT. Your children need this protection immediately.
feedback_messages.beneficiary_review: Your beneficiaries haven't been reviewed in {time_period}. This should be done annually.
feedback_messages.document_storage_issue: Your documents aren't properly stored or accessible. Create a storage plan today.
insights: Healthcare directive and financial POA protect you while LIVING—more immediately relevant than wills for young adults
Parents need guardian designations immediately regardless of age or assets
Beneficiary designations trump wills—review all designations annually
The cost of basic planning ($100-500) is trivial compared to probate costs (3-7% of estate)
Document location matters—families can't use documents they can't find
Update estate plans after: marriage, divorce, births, deaths, major asset changes
